rows: A shared live build module that proves the repository's start, address and stop, and writes the proven `live` block into `.afkv2/config.json`; the config reader returns that block.
The live build module is a shared producer: propose-verification, the end gate and the small lane all start the build through it, so it comes first.

A shared adapter that runs the judge and the grill's devil's-advocate pass as 1 headless call of the other provider's CLI, read-only, with the verdict schema (description before comparison), the fallback model and 1 transport retry.
The judge adapter stands alone and is used by the gate record, the end gate, the small lane and setup; its integration check needs a real codex and claude call.

A shared module that writes and verifies the gate record: runs with hashed evidence, the verdict, found bugs, the go of the small lane, the failed-run count, the proof lines and the proof comment text.
One reader and writer of the proof, shared by the end gate, the small lane and the ship step; it stores the verdict shape of 0002.
A new tracker port verb that posts 1 comment with attached pictures, on Jira (attachments, then an ADF comment) and on GitHub issues (`gh issue comment --attach`), keyed by the preview receipt.
A port verb with its own seam tests on 2 trackers; its live check needs gh 2.99.0 or later, and this machine has 2.92.0.
Move the generic draft, critique, reconcile engine out of propose-solution into a use-lavish proposer engine with a per-skill adapter; propose-solution becomes a thin caller with an unchanged CLI.
A move of tested code, kept apart from the new skill so a regression in propose-solution shows on its own.
The new skill `/afkv2:propose-verification`: 2 providers draft and critique a verification plan, the developer steers it on the page, the live build is proven, and the skill writes VERIFICATION.md.
The new skill writes VERIFICATION.md and owns its row format, which the plan rules then check.
The plan cut needs VERIFICATION.md, writes `> Rules: 2` and a Plan row column, and the plan check and start gate hold the row rules and the live-level rule for those plans only.
All plan-cut and plan-check rules move together behind the Rules 2 header, so old plans stay untouched in one place.
tdd_log takes the plan row, the test and the level per cycle; a no-test entry covers only its row; the done check refuses a subtask whose low-level rows are not green.
The per-row test-first record and the done check are one change of the subtask loop; it reads the Rules switch of 0007.

A new autopilot step after the last subtask: start the live build, run each high-level row once (a fail once more), call the judge when every row passed, write the gate record, send failed rows back, and stop after 3 failed gate runs.
The end gate joins the live build, the judge and the gate record after the subtask loop; it is the largest piece and stands alone.

create-change-request takes proofs per plan row and found bugs, mark-ready verifies the gate record before CI with or without a plan folder, the proof comment goes to the ticket after the developer's ship mark, and gc refuses a run branch whose comment is not posted.
Every ship-time change: proof payload, mark-ready, found bugs, the proof comment and the gc check read the same gate record.

The new skill `/afkv2:small-change` for a bug or a small enhancement: lane line, diagnosis loop for a bug, 1 page round, no code before the go, test-first fix, 1 high-level proof with before and after, the judge, and a stop that proposes the medium lane when the work grows.
The small lane reuses the engine, the gate record and the ship path, so it comes after them; it also carries the plain-chat trigger check.
Setup installs and proves Chrome DevTools MCP for both harnesses, names and proves the judge model per provider, and checks the gh floor when the tracker is GitHub.
Setup installs and proves the driver and the judge model; its live proof closes the 2 open questions of SDD §13.

The page engine shows a changed-this-round mark, fades older round chips, starts each card body with its heading, and exports a page diagram as the same picture into artifacts; the page guide asks for pictures wherever they help.
Page-engine changes touch no other subtask's files and can run at any point.
